metadata.title: PROJECT ATLAS — Deep Space & Galactic Catalogue
metadata.primarySource: NASA Science Hubble Messier Catalog & Galactic Structure Reference
metadata.disclaimer: 3D representations of nebulae, star clusters, and galaxies are artistic volumetric/particle visualizations grounded in verified astronomical distances, magnitudes, and dimensions, not direct 3D laser-scanned meshes.

milkyWay.name: Milky Way Galaxy

solarSystemDistanceFromCenterLy.note: Located in the Orion-Cygnus Arm (Local Spur)

milkyWay.centralObject: Sagittarius A* (Supermassive Black Hole at Galactic Center)
milkyWay.description: Our home galaxy is a barred spiral disk roughly 100,000 light-years across. The Solar System orbits the Galactic Center at ~26,000 light-years radius inside the Orion Spur, completing one galactic revolution every ~225–250 million years.

objects.name: Andromeda Galaxy
objects.dimensions: ~152,000 – 220,000 light-years across (Apparent angular size 6x full Moon)
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D spiral particle & volumetric disk representation
objects.description: Our nearest major galactic neighbor at 2.5 million light-years away. Hubble's panoramic mosaic resolved over 100 million stars and thousands of star clusters across its pancake-shaped spiral disk.

objects.name: Orion Nebula
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D multi-layered volumetric nebula cloud & Trapezium star cluster
objects.description: The closest large star-forming region to Earth (1,500 light-years), visible to the unaided eye below Orion's Belt. Its central cavity is illuminated by four massive young stars called the Trapezium cluster, and Hubble revealed numerous edge-on protoplanetary disks.

objects.name: Crab Nebula
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D filamentary shell & central pulsar jet visualization
objects.description: The expanding remnant of a bright supernova recorded by astronomers in 1054 AD, located 6,500 light-years away in Taurus. Charles Messier originally mistook it for Halley's Comet, inspiring him to compile his famous catalog.

objects.name: Eagle Nebula
objects.type: Emission Nebula (H II Region) & Open Cluster
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D star-forming cavity & ionized gas visualization
objects.description: An active star-forming emission nebula 7,000 light-years away in Serpens, where ultraviolet radiation from hot newborn stars is sculpting and eroding surrounding cold molecular gas clouds.

objects.name: Pillars of Creation
objects.type: Star-Forming Molecular Gas & Dust Columns (within Eagle Nebula)
objects.dimensions: Spire height ~4–5 light-years (adjacent M16 spire stretches 9.5 light-years)
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D volumetric columns with embedded protostars
objects.description: Iconic towering columns of cold interstellar hydrogen gas and dust inside Messier 16 (Eagle Nebula), imaged by Hubble and Webb in visible and infrared light to reveal infant stars forming within the pillars.

objects.name: Pleiades (Seven Sisters)
objects.type: Open Star Cluster with Reflection Nebulosity
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D hot B-type blue star cluster & wisps of reflection dust
objects.description: One of the nearest and brightest open star clusters at 445 light-years from Earth in Taurus, containing over 1,000 young stars illuminated by blue reflection nebulosity.

objects.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D grand-design spiral arms with companion galaxy NGC 5195
objects.description: Located 31 million light-years away, Messier 51's sweeping spiral arms act as star-forming factories compressed by the gravitational pull of its smaller yellowish companion galaxy, NGC 5195.

objects.name: Sombrero Galaxy
objects.type: Unbarred Spiral / Lenticular Galaxy with Prominent Dust Lane

distanceLy.display: 28 million light-years (28–30 Mly across Hubble/Webb studies)

objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D luminous central bulge & nearly edge-on dark dust ring
objects.description: Located 28 million light-years away in Virgo, M104 features a brilliant white bulbous core encircled by thick, nearly edge-on dark dust lanes and a rich system of globular clusters.

objects.name: Hercules Globular Cluster
objects.representationNote: Artistic 3D dense spherical star cluster particle representation
objects.description: Discovered by Edmond Halley in 1714, M13 is one of the brightest globular star clusters in the Northern Hemisphere, packing over 100,000 ancient stars into a sphere 25,000 light-years from Earth.
